issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Rideable.messageOnRide: The problem statement (UML and textual description) declares Rideable.messageOnRide() with no parameters returning a String and the template Main calls r.messageOnRide() with no arguments. In the solution repository, Rideable is declared as messageOnRide(int speed) and the implementing classes Pig and Seal implement messageOnRide(int). This parameter-list mismatch will cause compilation/use-site errors for students following the problem/template and is a blocking inconsistency.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the messageOnRide method signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution Rideable and its implementations to messageOnRide() with no parameters and return the string as specified (e.g., "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"). Alternatively, if a speed parameter is desired pedagogically, update the problem statement UML/text and the template Main to require and pass an int speed and document its meaning.

issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Farm.singFarmSongVerse: The problem statement UML declares singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal) with an Animal parameter, while the template Farm.java currently declares singFarmSongVerse with the parameter commented out (no formal parameter). The solution implements private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). The commented-out parameter in the template creates an inconsistency between template and problem description and may confuse students about the intended method signature and how to implement singFarmSong().
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template Farm.java with the problem statement: change the template method declaration to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) (uncomment/remove the commented-out parameter) so students implement the verse method consistently with the UML. If the no-arg design was intentional, update the problem statement UML/text to reflect a no-argument helper method instead.
